title: CloneSeq - Single-cell clonal 3D culture and analysis protocol
protocol: Cool down a box of 20 μL tips at −20°C before starting the encapsulation process.
Prepare MALDEX and PEGDT mix in a biological hood.
Keep the mixture on ice until use to prevent gelation.
Harvest ESC cells from tissue culture plate.
Wash the cells with 1× PBS and centrifuge at 500 rcf for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in 5 mL 1× PBS after washing again.
Pass cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Count and pellet 1×10^6 cells.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL 1× PBS with 10% Optiprep.
Add 20 μL ECM with cold tips to the cell suspension.
Transfer cell suspension to MALDEX mix.
Wash a magnetic stirring bar three times by 1× PBS.
Put the washed magnetic stirring bar into the MALDEX mix.
Prepare microfluidics setup.
Use 2000 mbar pump for carrier oil inlet, and 1000 mbar pump for PEGDT and MALDEX inlets.
Place the microfluidic device under the microscope.
Check for imperfections in the channels of the microfluidic device.
Ensure there are at least 3 mL of 2% HFE-7500 oil in the pressurized reservoir 15 mL tube.
Attach reagents and single cell suspension to the corresponding pressure controllers.
Make sure tubing reaches the bottom of the tubes.
Connect the cell mixer to the power supply.
Add ice to the ice stand for MALDEX mix.
Prepare two 2 mL collection tubes in a cooling block.
Turn on the pressure controllers.
Open the A-i-O control software and change all flow rate units to μL/h.
Set scale factors: oil inlet to 4.3, MALDEX inlet to 1.1, PEGDT inlet to 1.
Apply maximum pressure to each inlet tubing before connecting to the device.
Connect tubing to the microfluidic device according to specified positions.
Place outlet tubing into a collection tube.
Press “edit mode” in A-i-O software and switch to "pressure mode".
Set parameters: oil 200 mbar, PEGDT 100 mbar, MALDEX 100 mbar.
Press “edit mode” again to start all inlets simultaneously.
Wait until drops are formed properly at the junction of three flows.
Change flow rates as follows: oil 2000 μL/h, PEG 500 μL/h, DEX 500 μL/h.
Transfer the collection tubes to a 37°C incubator for at least 5 min to stabilize the formation of the hydrogel.
Transfer the upper part of the collection to the drop breaking solution.
Mix by gently inverting the tubes.
Incubate for exactly 1 min in the 37°C incubator.
Discard the lower oil fraction.
Add 1 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge at 250 rcf for 2.5 min.
Discard the upper PBS fraction and the lower oil fraction.
Wash two more times with 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Resuspend the beads in 500 μL pre-warmed ESC medium.
Transfer to a well in a 48-well plate.
Wash the collection tube with 500 μL pre-warmed ESC medium.
Transfer to a different well. Repeat twice.
Check the clone formation status every day after collection.
Collect hydrogel spheres from all three wells into a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 250 rcf for 2.5 min.
Remove the old medium and wash once with 1× PBS.
Resuspend the hydrogel with pre-warmed cell medium (500 μL) in a new well.
Incubate single clone suspension with dextranase by 1:20 dilution at 37°C for 30 min to dissolve PEGDT-MALDEX hydrogel.
Gently mix the clone suspension.
Pass the mixture through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Place the tube in a 37°C incubator.
Let clones settle by gravity for 30 minutes.
Gently remove the upper medium layer.
Replace with 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Wash the clone suspensions using a pipette.
Repeat the PBS wash once more.
Resuspend the clone suspension in 200 μL of 1× PBS after washing.
Count 2 μL of the suspension using a hemocytometer to determine the concentration of clones.
Resuspend the clones in 1× PBS containing 10% Optiprep at a final concentration of 10,000 clones/mL.
Wash a magnetic stirring bar three times in 1× PBS.
Place the washed stirring bar into the cell suspension.
Prepare the RT lysis mix.
Filter the hydrogel barcoding beads solution through a 70 μm strainer to remove aggregates and debris.
Centrifuge the filtered hydrogel barcoding bead solution at 1500 rcf for 1 minute.
Discard the buffer above the pellet of barcode beads.
Prepare the microfluidics setup.
Install pressure controller as specified.
Set 69 mbar pump for carrier oil inlet.
Set 345 mbar pump for RT lysis mix inlet.
Set pumps for cell and barcode bead inlets accordingly.
Use pressurized reservoir with appropriate tube sizes.
Utilize 1.5 mL Eppendorf Safe-Lock microcentrifuge tubes for RT lysis and hydrogel barcoding beads.
Use 2 mL Eppendorf Safe-Lock microcentrifuge tube for cell suspension.
Employ 15 mL tube for 2% HFE-7500 oil.
Operate cell mixer with ice stand in place.
Place magnetic stirring bar inside the tube to agitate cells and prevent sedimentation.
Select flow unit size M for barcode inlet.
Choose flow unit size S for other inlets.
Position microfluidic device according to specified inlet positions.
Connect 2% HFE-7500 oil to inlet position (1).
Connect outlet for collection at positions (3) and (4).
Insert single clone suspension into position (4).
Inject RT lysis mix into position (5).
Place collection plate in cooling block.
Initialize control software for microscope operation.
Put a microfluidic device under the microscope.
Check its channels for imperfections.
Ensure there are at least 2 mL 2% HFE-7500 oil in the pressurized reservoir 15 mL tube.
Attach all reagents (lysis, barcodes, oil) and single clone suspension to the corresponding pressure controller.
Make sure that the tubing reaches the bottom of the tubes.
Connect the cell mixer to the power supply.
Add ice to the ice stand for cells.
Prepare collection plate: take a 96-well plate, for each sample prepare 4 wells for collection by adding 50 μL 2% HFE-7500 oil in the well.
Turn on the pressure controllers.
Open the A-i-O control software.
Change all the flow rate units to μL/h.
Set scale factors for different inlets: 4.3 for oil, 1 for RT lysis mix and single clone suspension.
Apply maximum pressure before connecting tubing to the device to push liquid to the end of tubing.
Stop the pressure after pushing the liquid.
Connect tubing to the microfluidic device according to specified positions.
Put the outlet tubing into a collection tube.
In A-i-O software, press “edit mode” and set parameters: oil 69 mbar, lysis 27 mbar, cell 27 mbar, barcode 100 mbar.
Press “edit mode” again to start all inlets simultaneously.
Wait until observing the boundary between cell suspension and RT lysis mix flows at the junction where drops are formed.
Keep oil and barcode inlets in pressure mode.
Control oil flow rate around 350 μL/h and barcode beads flow rate around 35-40 μL/h.
Change to flow rate mode for cell and lysis control: set cell flow rate between 50–120 μL/h, and lysis flow rate between 70–120 μL/h.
Ensure lysis flow rate equals the cell flow rate to ensure sufficient RT reaction mix for transcriptome.
Take a short video to estimate encapsulation efficiency.
Count the number of events of one clone and one barcode in one drop and divide by time.
Put the collection tube into the collection well plate after having stable drops.
Count the time of collection to estimate the number of events per collection.
Collect around 350 clones per well.
Stop the pump upon termination of the run.
Place the collection plate under a UV lamp for 10 minutes, keeping it about 3–5 cm below the lamp.
Take a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf safe-lock tube and add 1 mL T10E0.1T0.1 buffer.
Push all the buffer through the tubing used for barcodes and collect in the tube with unused barcodes.
Wrap the tube containing unused barcodes with aluminum foil.
Transfer the collection plate to a PCR machine for reverse transcription (RT).
Pause point: store cDNA at −20°C for up to 1 week.
